mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 2.5% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 2.5%; or IC < -0.05 in all post-trigger windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 3.5% predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor-market disengagement reduces corporate optimism and consumer spending.
regime_hint: Elevated unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: Over 20-day rolling window, positive 5-day returns occur when UNRATE > 3.5%; or IC > 0.1 in all such windows.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP Chained) exceeds INDPRO by more than 10% for two consecutive months, it indicates strong demand relative to supply, leading to a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO by at least 8% for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, resulting in a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥ 8% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Manufacturing contraction or weak GDP growth
failure_condition: In regimes matching the trigger, 20-day forward returns are non-negative more than 40% of the time; or IC > 0.05 over rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL below 300 (monthly, index 1982-84=100) followed by a subsequent rise signals the Fed's disinflationary stance, producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses below 300 and then crosses above 300 within the same month
failure_condition: Over 12 months post-trigger, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than a control group (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 by 10% for two consecutive months, it reflects labor market strength that supports corporate investment and drives a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 165,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In such regimes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (IC ≤ 0.05) across multiple testing windows.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in HOUST (housing starts) by at least 15% predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced capital spending and consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥ 15% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20-day windows, positive 5-day returns occur when HOUST declines by ≥ 15% for two months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 12% in a month compared to the prior month, it indicates supply-side softness that precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return in consumer-discretionary sectors.
failure_condition: In such regimes, 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (IC ≤ -0.1) across multiple testing periods.
